Their overlap is limited to the general subject of military medals and routine award-administration language, which is insufficient to establish a material drafting template.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The decoration of the Legion of Merit shall be awarded by the President of the United States or at his direction","parent_excerpt":"The Secretary of the Navy shall award the Purple Heart, in the name of the President of the United States","explanation":"C16 has superficially parallel presidential award language, but assigns a different decoration through a different authority structure and does not reproduce the child's proposal, degree, or foreign-award procedures."},{"child_excerpt":"Awards of the decoration of the Legion of Merit may be proposed to the President by the Secretary of the Army, the Secretary of the Navy, and the Secretary of the Air Force","parent_excerpt":"for award, under such regulations as the Secretaries of the Army, Navy, and Air Force ... may severally prescribe","explanation":"C06 names the same service secretaries in administering a military medal, but its regulation-coordination scheme is not the child's nomination-and-approval process."},{"child_excerpt":"The decoration of the Legion of Merit ... shall be awarded ... to members of the armed forces","parent_excerpt":"Such medal may be awarded ... to those enlisted men of the Army of the United States and the United States Air Force","explanation":"C20 shares only generic medal-eligibility phrasing and supplies no comparable decisional machinery."}]}
